requirements.text: All operations that create, modify or delete registry content or metadata MUST use a SecureChannel with `MessageSecurityMode` `SignAndEncrypt`. This includes get-or-create Calls, file write Opens, Writes and committing Closes, label and native-document mutations, deletion and domain Methods that change registry state. Roles and Permissions apply independently. Reads SHOULD use a secured channel. Deployment policy MAY permit read-only operations and event subscriptions over `None`, but clients MUST NOT infer authenticity, integrity or confidentiality from such a connection.

requirements.text: `Xid` MUST always be the structural relative xRegistry path of the registry, group, Resource or Version. The logical Resource `Xid` is its resource path. Each exact Version `Xid` is that Resource `Xid` followed by `/versions/<VID>`. An `Xid` MUST NOT be a content fingerprint, digest or other document-derived identifier. A server MAY use content identity as an internal lookup, cache or deduplication fast path, but that optimization MUST NOT change `Xid`, `Subject`, `ResourceId`, `VersionId` or AddressSpace placement.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.2. Resolving xRegistry `xid`s to OPC UA nodes

requirements.text: Document-backed servers MUST preserve the distinct Resource/Version hierarchy. A missing `Versions` component MUST NOT cause a client to treat Group children as exact Versions. The client instead applies the declared metadata-only, local-xref or remote-proxy contract, or reports an unsupported mapping. It MUST NOT guess a different hierarchy from missing nodes.

requirements.text: For omitted mutable Properties, `Labels` entries and Resource Meta `MetaLabels` entries, the server MUST delete, reset to default or leave unchanged only as Core or server-managed semantics specify.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.3. Entity processing rules

requirements.text: Partial update MUST NOT patch arbitrary bytes inside a Resource document. Document changes replace the complete byte stream.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.3. Entity processing rules

requirements.text: A server MUST apply Core's entity-level atomicity rule. A native `WriteDocument` or `ApplyChanges` validates the complete resulting entity before committing it. A sequence of separate create, Property Write and file Calls is a sequence of interactions, not one atomic replacement. If an implementation cannot provide the requested atomic entity operation, it MUST reject it rather than advertise a weaker equivalent. Atomicity across separate entities follows Core and the declared batch contract.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.3. Entity processing rules

requirements.text: [Nested collection processing](https://github.com/xregistry/spec/blob/v1.0-rc4/core/spec.md#updating-nested-registry-collections) MUST process only the nested collection entries. It MUST NOT modify the owning entity's Properties. For example, processing Resources under a selected Group creates or updates `ResourceType` children without changing that Group's Properties.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.3. Entity processing rules

requirements.text: Unless otherwise stated, the server MUST ignore an update to a read-only Property only when xRegistry defines that behavior for the attribute. Otherwise it MUST reject the Write with `Bad_NotWritable` or `Bad_UserAccessDenied`. If a supplied identifier Property (`RegistryId`, `GroupId`, `ResourceId` or `VersionId`) conflicts with the target entity, the request MUST fail with `Bad_InvalidArgument` or `Bad_IdentityChangeNotSupported`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.3. Entity processing rules

requirements.text: On a committed Registry, Group or Version change, the server MUST update the entity's `ModifiedAt` and increment its `Epoch`. A Resource Meta change updates `MetaModifiedAt` and increments `MetaEpoch` instead. The selected default Version's `Epoch` and `ModifiedAt` remain unchanged unless Version attributes also change.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.3. Entity processing rules

requirements.text: On creation, the server MUST initialize the applicable `CreatedAt`, `ModifiedAt`, `Epoch`, `MetaCreatedAt`, `MetaModifiedAt`, `MetaEpoch`, `Xid` and identifier Properties under Core and the Version 0.11.0 companion's auto-bootstrap rules.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.4. OPC UA-specific attribute processing

requirements.text: OPC UA represents fixed metadata as typed Property Values: strings use `String`, timestamps use `DateTime`, `ExternalReference` uses `ExpandedNodeId`, and `Epoch` and `MetaEpoch` use `UInt32`. The xRegistry `labels` are string-valued Property Variables under `Labels`, or under `MetaLabels` for Resource Meta. Extension attributes are not labels: a native document view preserves their JSON kinds and values through `RegistryValueDataType` subtypes, while a domain mapping uses its declared UA DataTypes. Neither representation MAY stringify typed values to fit an `AttributesType` container.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.4. OPC UA-specific attribute processing

requirements.text: An xRegistry `epoch` is an unsigned integer in the range 0 through 4,294,967,295. Before a mutation increments one or more `Epoch` or `MetaEpoch` values, the Server MUST check every affected counter. If any counter is at the maximum, the operation MUST fail with `Bad_OutOfRange`, make no state change and emit no event.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.4. OPC UA-specific attribute processing

requirements.text: For a Resource document read, clients obtain accompanying metadata from the logical Resource's delegated Version Properties and authoritative Resource Meta Properties. For an exact Version, they read that Version Object's metadata. A server MAY combine these reads in a domain Method. The interoperable baseline uses separate `Open` /`Read`/`Close` operations and Browse/Read for metadata.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.4. OPC UA-specific attribute processing

requirements.text: The xRegistry `contenttype` attribute maps to `ContentType`, not `MimeType`. The inherited `FileType` Property `MimeType` MAY mirror `ContentType` for generic FileTransfer clients. If both are present, `ContentType` represents the xRegistry attribute; `MimeType` is the FileTransfer media hint.

requirements.text: Registries, Groups and exact Versions MAY expose `Labels`. Resource Meta owns `MetaLabels`, which is authoritative on the logical Resource. Clients call attribute Methods on the container that owns the attribute.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.5. Method signatures and argument mapping

requirements.text: The OPTIONAL native-document capability is separate from label Methods. `ReadDocument` returns a typed native view; `WriteDocument` and `ApplyChanges` update typed values through the same validation, authorization, epoch and atomic-commit rules as compatibility writes. `OpenDocument`, `ReadDocumentPart` and `CloseDocument` provide a pinned bounded view when `XREG-NativeSnapshots` is supported. These Methods do not replace the raw `Capabilities` or `Model` FileType interfaces.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.5. Method signatures and argument mapping

requirements.text: The owning Registry exposes this capability as `TypedAccess`. `ReadDocument` takes one `RegistryReadRequestDataType` and returns one `RegistryReadResultDataType`. `TargetXid` selects the entity, `DocumentKind` selects metadata, model or capabilities, and `View` selects the complete generic value (`0`) or named fields (`1`). A client MUST check the returned `StatusCode` and `Issues` as well as the Call result. Metadata reads return the selected entity's epoch; Registry, model and capability reads return the Registry epoch. Missing entity revision information MUST NOT be replaced by the Registry epoch.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.5. Method signatures and argument mapping

requirements.text: Native records preserve authored presence through `PresentFields`, and unknown members through `AdditionalFields`. An absent member differs from explicit null, false or an empty collection. Generic numbers retain their exact coefficient and exponent rather than rounding through Double. `ApplyChanges` uses native member/array path elements, not JSON Pointer strings. A missing parent path is an error. A no-op native update MUST preserve the retained raw bytes and epochs.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.5. Method signatures and argument mapping

requirements.text: Native continuation tokens bind the selection, revision and authorization view. A client MUST NOT treat a partial named record as a complete document. For documents that cannot fit in one response, including one oversized nested value, complete native access uses `OpenDocument`, `ReadDocumentPart` and `CloseDocument`. A successful Open returns a Session-bound `SnapshotId`, `TargetEpoch` and `RegistryEpoch`. `ReadDocumentPart` traverses native fields or array indexes and reads bounded leaf ranges under `SnapshotLimits`; it does not require reconstructing JSON. Clients MUST check each result, use positive item/byte limits and release the snapshot when finished. Authorization changes invalidate snapshots. An invalid handle or token fails with `Bad_InvalidState`; capacity and encoding failures remain explicit. This pinned native view is not a retained publication or a snapshot of remote providers or domain file bytes.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.5. Method signatures and argument mapping

requirements.text: Every `ExpectedEpoch` argument in the declared label and Delete signatures is REQUIRED. A client supplies `0` when it does not request the comparison; Core's omission of an epoch precondition does not omit a UA Method argument.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.5. Method signatures and argument mapping / 4.5.1. Concurrency and locking

requirements.text: To mutate Registry, Group or Version labels through `Labels.AddAttribute` and `Labels.RemoveAttribute`, the client supplies that entity's current `Epoch` as `ExpectedEpoch`, under the [Core epoch precondition](https://github.com/xregistry/spec/blob/v1.0-rc4/core/spec.md#epoch-flag). If the supplied value is non-zero and unequal, the Method MUST fail with `Bad_InvalidState` and make no change. On success, `Epoch` increments and `ModifiedAt` is updated.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.5. Method signatures and argument mapping / 4.5.1. Concurrency and locking

requirements.text: To mutate Resource Meta labels through `MetaLabels.AddAttribute` and `MetaLabels.RemoveAttribute`, the client supplies the current `MetaEpoch` as `ExpectedEpoch`. If the supplied value is non-zero and unequal, the Method MUST fail with `Bad_InvalidState` and make no change. On success, `MetaEpoch` increments and `MetaModifiedAt` is updated. For either container, `ExpectedEpoch = 0` disables the check.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.5. Method signatures and argument mapping / 4.5.1. Concurrency and locking

requirements.text: For document replacement, exclusive `Open(write)` serializes file writers, but FileType has no `ExpectedEpoch` argument. Separate epoch Reads and an Open/Write/Close sequence do not establish an atomic epoch precondition, particularly when metadata can change independently. A client requiring that precondition MUST use a documented operation or lock that enforces it at commit, or report the requested operation as unsupported. It MUST NOT present an unchecked file replacement as an epoch-matched one.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.5. Method signatures and argument mapping / 4.5.1. Concurrency and locking

requirements.text: Every logical Resource handle MUST remain pinned to the exact Version selected at `Open`. A later default-Version switch affects only later opens. Logical and exact opens MUST share the same exact-Version writer reservation and an incarnation safeguard, so deletion and recreation of the same Version identity cannot let a stale handle commit into the replacement Object.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.5. Method signatures and argument mapping / 4.5.1. Concurrency and locking

requirements.text: For deletion, a client passes the current group or exact Version `Epoch`, or the current logical Resource `MetaEpoch`, as `ExpectedEpoch`. If a non-zero value does not equal the applicable value, the Method Call MUST fail with `Bad_InvalidState`, delete nothing and produce no partial effects. An `ExpectedEpoch` of `0` disables the check. Deletion is therefore an atomic epoch-matched Method call rather than a read-then-delete sequence.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.5. Method signatures and argument mapping / 4.5.1. Concurrency and locking

requirements.text: A server MAY expose coarser-grained exclusive access through the standard OPC UA locking mechanism, a `LockingServicesType` component (`InitLock` / `RenewLock` / `ExitLock` / `BreakLock`, OPC 10000-5) on the Registry root, a Group or a Resource. This lets a client hold an explicit exclusive lock across a multi-step create/update sequence. This API does not require locking. Without it, clients rely on FileTransfer `Open` exclusivity and `Epoch` preconditions.

requirements.text: The table above is authoritative for fixed and system Properties. A client mapping a model-defined Property BrowseName to an xRegistry attribute name MUST convert only ASCII uppercase letters (`A` through `Z`) to their lowercase counterparts. For a Resource Meta Property, the client MUST first remove the exact, case-sensitive `Meta` prefix. A client mapping a field of a structured `ExtensionObject` to an xRegistry attribute MUST apply the same ASCII conversion to the field name; it MUST NOT remove a `Meta` prefix from the field name. No other character is changed, and Unicode case folding MUST NOT be applied. The resulting attribute name MUST satisfy Core's attribute-name grammar.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.6. Attribute mapping

requirements.text: If two distinct Properties on the same entity map to the same xRegistry attribute path in the selected representation, including a collision with a mapping in the table above, the client's read MUST fail as ambiguous. It MUST NOT select a Property by Browse order or another tie-breaker.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.6. Attribute mapping

requirements.text: The xRegistry attributes `self`, collection `url` attributes, collection `count` attributes, `metaurl`, `versionsurl`, `versionscount`, `defaultversionurl`, `isdefault`, `ancestorid`, `<RESOURCE>` and `<RESOURCE>base64` are serialization artifacts or domain/model attributes rather than mandatory base Properties. A server MAY expose them as domain Properties, but a client MUST only derive them when the selected mapping supplies the necessary state. It MUST NOT infer ancestry or default selection from Browse order. Serialized URLs and local pointers follow §8.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.6. Attribute mapping

requirements.text: Registry, Group, Version and Resource Meta labels are enumerated by Browsing `Labels` or `MetaLabels` and Reading each `<Attribute>` Property Variable. Clients change these string labels by calling the owning container's `AddAttribute` or `RemoveAttribute` Method with the epoch described in §4.5.1. Typed extension attributes use the native document or domain mapping; they MUST NOT be coerced into label strings. Both label containers are deleted with their owning entity.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.7. Supported operations discovery and pagination

requirements.text: A server MUST NOT require a side-effecting operation for discovery. If a FileTransfer Method, `CreateGroup`, `GetOrCreateGroup`, `CreateResource`, `GetOrCreateResource`, an applicable `Labels` or `MetaLabels` object, or its `AddAttribute` /`RemoveAttribute` Method is absent, non-executable or rejected with `Bad_UserAccessDenied`, the corresponding xRegistry write capability is not available to that client.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.7. Supported operations discovery and pagination

requirements.text: For file bytes, a client paginates through `Read(fileHandle, length)` and MAY use `GetPosition` and `SetPosition` to implement random access. For labels, a client browses `Labels` or `MetaLabels` and pages with normal Browse continuation points where needed.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 4. The OPC UA API access model / 4.7. Supported operations discovery and pagination

requirements.text: A federation selector needs every necessary Browse page, not just a client-selected page. A client MUST call `BrowseNext` until no continuation point remains before claiming no match or a unique match. On early termination it MUST release outstanding continuation points when the Session is usable. A failed or expired continuation point MUST NOT yield a complete collection.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.1. Reading the registry

requirements.text: The base Properties include `RegistryId`, `SpecVersion`, `CapabilitiesSnapshot`, `CapabilitiesInfo`, `Xid`, `Epoch`, OPTIONAL `Name`, `Description`, `Documentation`, `CreatedAt` and `ModifiedAt`. `Capabilities` and `Model` are `FileType` component Objects, and `Labels` is an `AttributesType` Object. `CapabilitiesSnapshot` is REQUIRED only for the corresponding companion conformance unit; `CapabilitiesInfo` remains an OPTIONAL partial convenience view.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.2. Creating and updating the registry

requirements.text: A full Registry replacement writes the complete set of replacement mutable `RegistryType` Properties. Core rules determine which omitted mutable attributes are removed or reset. The `Capabilities` and `Model` components are `FileType` Objects. Their absence MUST NOT require a change. If present, the server MUST write each as a complete replacement document through `Open(write)` /`Write`/`Close`, unless it supports finer-grained updates. When raw `Capabilities` JSON changes, the Server MUST publish any typed capabilities view from the same committed revision and authorization view. It MUST NOT use `CapabilitiesInfo` to replace fields absent from that partial view.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.2. Creating and updating the registry

requirements.text: A partial Registry update writes only included Properties. Included label changes use `Labels.AddAttribute` or `Labels.RemoveAttribute`; typed extension changes use `NativeRegistryAccessType.ApplyChanges` or the domain mapping. For null and removal, the Server applies Core's attribute-specific deletion or reset semantics. It removes a label with `Labels.RemoveAttribute` or a typed extension with a native `Remove` change. It MUST fail with `Bad_NotSupported` if the attribute is mandatory or cannot be removed. A native `Set` change containing `RegistryNullValueDataType` stores an explicit null member, while a native `Remove` deletes it. A native `Set` MUST NOT reinterpret that value as Core's removal request.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.2. Creating and updating the registry

requirements.text: When the requested operation is explicitly limited to group collection processing, registry-level attributes MUST be rejected with `Bad_InvalidArgument`, corresponding to xRegistry `groups_only`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.3. Exporting the registry

requirements.text: Export serializes the selected `RegistryType` subtree into Core JSON document view. The baseline algorithm browses the subtree, reads mapped Properties and requested model/capabilities, and uses Open/Read/Close for each included, document-bearing Version under §5.13.1. The exporter MUST NOT read fabricated documents for metadata-only Resources or expand local `xref` targets. Section 8 defines serialization and capture limitations.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.3. Exporting the registry

requirements.text: A server MAY expose a domain Method or Property to optimize export. Its output MUST have the same document shape as the baseline algorithm. Implementations support import through normal create/update operations or a domain-defined import Method.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.4. Reading capabilities and model documents

requirements.text: `CapabilitiesInfo` retains its existing `RegistryCapabilitiesDataType` layout as an OPTIONAL, application-supplied partial convenience view. It is not a mapping of Core's canonical capabilities schema. A resolver MUST NOT infer an enabled capability from an old field name or treat an absent convenience field as a Core default. It MUST use `CapabilitiesSnapshot` for the canonical typed standard fields and the raw document for fields the typed view does not represent. Every FileType read in this section follows §5.13.1.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.4. Reading capabilities and model documents

requirements.text: Raw and typed observations MUST describe the same committed revision and authorization view when presented as a matching pair. A raw capabilities Open pins that revision and view for the handle. Independently sampled reads do not prove correspondence. If a consistent typed observation is unavailable, the server MUST report that explicitly. It MUST NOT fill absent standard fields with defaults, truncate an oversized typed value or make the raw file unreadable because the typed value exceeds an encoding limit.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.4. Reading capabilities and model documents

requirements.text: The base model defines no separate `CapabilitiesOffered` Property. A server supporting mutable capabilities MUST expose offered-capabilities information inside `Capabilities` JSON, in a domain subtype Property, or through domain documentation referenced by `Model`. Without an exposed target, an offered-capabilities read MUST fail with `Bad_NodeIdUnknown` or `Bad_NotSupported`; it does not invent an unmapped base node.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.4. Reading capabilities and model documents

requirements.text: A client reads the full xRegistry model definition through the `RegistryType.Model` `FileType` component Object. It calls `Open` for read, repeats `Read` until it has the complete JSON byte stream, then calls `Close`. Before browsing entities, clients MAY use this definition to map domain collection names to `GroupType` and `ResourceType` subtype BrowseNames. The Version 0.11.0 companion also offers typed named and generic native-document views through `NativeRegistryAccessType`; those views complement rather than replace the raw FileType document.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.4. Reading capabilities and model documents

requirements.text: The base model defines no distinct `ModelSource` Property. If a server distinguishes the effective model from the client-provided source, it MUST expose that source in a domain subtype Property or a documented shape inside `Model` JSON. If a model-source target exists but its source has never been set, the server MUST return an empty JSON object (`{}`) as its JSON content, under xRegistry semantics.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.5. Updating capabilities and model-source information

requirements.text: Unsupported capability changes MUST fail with `Bad_InvalidArgument` or `Bad_NotSupported`. File writes stage changes until a successful committing `Close`; the capabilities governing an interaction MUST NOT change while that interaction is being processed.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.5. Updating capabilities and model-source information

requirements.text: Model-source updates need a domain-defined target or operation; the base API defines no writable `ModelSource` node. A server accepting these updates through its `RegistryType.Model` `FileType` component Object MUST document that `Model` serves as model source. It MUST apply xRegistry full-replacement rules through `Open(mode = 6)`/`Write`/`Close`. If it exposes only effective `Model`, an attempt to write model source MUST fail with `Bad_NotWritable` or `Bad_NotSupported`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.6. Listing group collections

requirements.text: To list a Group collection, a client selects the domain's collection view. It browses `GroupType` children of the selected `RegistryType` root in the direct layout, or of its `GroupCollectionType` view when that facet is used. The client checks `CollectionName` where declared and keeps Groups with the same ID in different collections distinct. Group collections are unordered maps keyed by identifier. Browse returns children in server-defined order; the client MUST NOT infer collection order from Browse position.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.7. Creating and updating groups

requirements.text: Groups are `GroupType` entries in the selected Group collection. For a direct single-collection layout, the base creation sequence is as follows. For each Group key, the preferred one-shot operation is `GetOrCreateGroup(GroupId)` on `RegistryType`. It returns an existing Group with `Created = false` or creates one with `Created = true`. When an existing Group MUST cause failure, the client uses strict `CreateGroup(GroupId)`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.7. Creating and updating groups

requirements.text: The base Methods carry no collection-name argument. A multi-collection domain that supports creation MUST define an unambiguous collection-qualified creation operation or use its native registration mapping. A client MUST NOT select a collection by guessing which existing Group shares the supplied ID.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.7. Creating and updating groups

requirements.text: If a group does not exist and the operation permits creation, the server creates it with `GetOrCreateGroup` or strict `CreateGroup` on the registry root. The supplied group identifier MUST match `GroupId`. A mismatch fails with `Bad_InvalidArgument`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.7. Creating and updating groups

requirements.text: If an operation attempts to update group-level attributes while it is explicitly limited to nested resource collection processing, the server MUST reject it with `Bad_InvalidArgument`, corresponding to xRegistry `resources_only`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.8. Reading a group

requirements.text: The standard base Properties are `GroupId`, `Xid`, `Epoch`, `Name`, `Description`, `Documentation`, `CreatedAt` and `ModifiedAt`. `Labels` is an `AttributesType` Object. Domain group subtypes MAY add mandatory group-key Properties and extension metadata.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.9. Deleting groups

requirements.text: If an entity-specific `epoch` precondition is supplied for deletion, the client MUST pass it as `ExpectedEpoch`. If `ExpectedEpoch` is non-zero and does not equal the group's current `Epoch`, the Call MUST fail with `Bad_InvalidState` and delete nothing. `ExpectedEpoch = 0` disables the check.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.10. Resource metadata and resource documents

requirements.text: If the Resource type's xRegistry model declares `hasdocument = false`, document access MUST fail with `Bad_NotReadable`, `Bad_InvalidState` or `Bad_NotSupported`. Metadata remains the normal entity representation. A federation resolver reports `unsupported_operation` for that model-level condition before attempting FileTransfer.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.10. Resource metadata and resource documents

requirements.text: For a domain using `MetadataResourceType`, clients Browse and Read metadata Properties or open its read-only `Metadata` FileType for the JSON metadata representation. They MUST NOT Open the Resource Object itself as a file. `HasDocument` is false and `MaxVersions` is 1. Its sole metadata Version can be selected using the observed `VersionId`; selection of a different Version MUST fail rather than substitute the current value. If the server assigns that sole identifier, it MUST NOT add an unauthored `versionid` to retained raw metadata or native `PresentFields`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.10. Resource metadata and resource documents

requirements.text: The `Metadata` handle pins a committed revision and authorization view. Typed Properties are read-only projections, not a separate mutation path. They and native documents MUST preserve the admitted metadata's exact values and presence, including unknown extensions, array order and numeric precision. Raw-originated metadata retains its bytes; native-originated metadata uses deterministic compatibility serialization. The server MUST reject malformed UTF-8, duplicate JSON member names and non-finite numbers rather than coerce them into another admitted value. An oversized typed read MUST fail explicitly without making raw metadata unavailable. The same representation rules apply to Group metadata in that domain.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.10. Resource metadata and resource documents

requirements.text: A domain mapping that instead uses `ResourceType` for metadata-only state MUST document its representation. Inherited FileType members still follow their OPC UA ModellingRules, but their presence does not establish that a domain document exists. A `Size` value of zero alone MUST NOT turn a metadata-only Resource into an empty document. This rule includes the `categories` / `registries` catalog model.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.10. Resource metadata and resource documents

requirements.text: Clients obtain Resource metadata by reading file Properties before or after the document bytes, not through transport headers. Servers SHOULD keep `ContentType` consistent with the inherited `MimeType` so generic FileTransfer clients can identify the media type.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.10. Resource metadata and resource documents

requirements.text: If an explicitly mapped `ResourceUrl` or draft `ExternalReference` supplies the document, `Open` MAY fail with `Bad_NotReadable` or MAY return a local cached representation, as advertised by the implementation. These mechanisms remain distinct as specified in §10.3. A generic `Bad_NotReadable` without such a declaration is not a redirect instruction.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.11. Listing resource collections

requirements.text: To list a Resource collection, the client browses its `GroupType` folder for logical `ResourceType` or `MetadataResourceType` children, as declared by the requested domain collection. Exact Version Objects are not Group children and MUST NOT appear in this Browse. Resource collections are unordered maps keyed by identifier. Since Browse returns children in server-defined order, a client MUST NOT infer collection order from Browse position.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.12. Creating and updating resources

requirements.text: The owning `GroupType` provides Resource creation and update. For each Resource key, the preferred one-shot operation is `GetOrCreateResource(ResourceId, VersionId, RequestFileOpen)` on `GroupType`. It returns the exact Version NodeId and `AssignedVersionId`, with `Created = false` for an existing Version or `Created = true` for a new one. If `RequestFileOpen = true`, the returned write handle is pinned to that exact Version and MAY be used immediately.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.12. Creating and updating resources

requirements.text: For a new Resource, the logical Resource, `Versions` component and first Version commit atomically in one xRegistry operation. To create a Version of an existing Resource, the client supplies its `ResourceId` and a new or server-assigned `VersionId`. When an existing `(ResourceId, VersionId)` MUST cause failure, the client uses strict `CreateResource(ResourceId, VersionId, RequestFileOpen)`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.12. Creating and updating resources

requirements.text: For mutable default-Version metadata updates, the client MAY use the logical Resource's delegated Properties and `Labels` or target the selected exact Version directly. Both paths update the exact Version against its `Epoch`. Resource Meta updates instead write Resource Meta Properties and call `MetaLabels.AddAttribute` /`MetaLabels.RemoveAttribute` on the logical Resource against `MetaEpoch`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.12. Creating and updating resources

requirements.text: If the supplied `ResourceId` conflicts with the selected resource identifier, the operation MUST fail with `Bad_InvalidArgument`. If supplied `VersionId` creates a new version rather than replacing the default version, the operation MUST follow §5.18.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.13. Reading a resource document

requirements.text: The client MAY reproduce Resource response metadata by reading the logical Resource's delegated `Size`, `Writable`, `MimeType`, `LastModifiedTime`, `ContentType`, `ResourceId`, `VersionId` and `Epoch`. It reads Resource Meta from the logical Resource's `MetaEpoch`, `MetaLabels`, `MetaCreatedAt`, `MetaModifiedAt` and domain meta Properties.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.13. Reading a resource document

requirements.text: If `ResourceUrl` or `ExternalReference` identifies external content, the server MAY serve cached bytes from the local file or redirect through metadata. For the latter, it returns readable `ResourceUrl` /`ExternalReference` and fails `Open` with a suitable StatusCode. The server MUST document its choice in `Capabilities`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.13. Reading a resource document / 5.13.1. FileTransfer read lifecycle

requirements.text: The baseline read uses the [FileType Methods][ua-filetype] on the selected file Object. A Method's ObjectId and MethodId MUST identify that Object and its actual Method node. A BrowseName shown here is not a numeric MethodId. This procedure also applies to `Model`, `Capabilities` and a namespace file.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.13. Reading a resource document / 5.13.1. FileTransfer read lifecycle

requirements.text: 4. Continue after a short, nonempty Read. Part 20 permits fewer bytes than requested. An empty ByteString indicates end-of-file. A known, reliable `Size` can also establish the total, but a premature end or a size change MUST invalidate a complete-capture claim. Unknown size requires an end-of-file observation. A successful zero-byte file still has an Open/Read/Close lifecycle.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.13. Reading a resource document / 5.13.1. FileTransfer read lifecycle

requirements.text: 5. Call `Close(fileHandle)` when finished. After every successful Open, the client MUST attempt Close on success, error, cancellation or limit exhaustion while the Session is usable. A failed Open does not allocate a handle to close. Session loss invalidates the handle. Reconnecting requires a new Open, not reuse of that handle or file position.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.13. Reading a resource document / 5.13.1. FileTransfer read lifecycle

requirements.text: The client MUST NOT use a handle on another Object, in another Session or after Close. It MUST retain the original read error if cleanup also fails and report the cleanup failure as additional diagnostic information. A client MUST NOT report unsuccessful cleanup as an entirely successful sequence. A range read via `SetPosition` is not a complete export unless every needed byte has been accounted for. [§11](#11-error-handling) maps StatusCodes and [§11.1](#111-federation-resolver-outcomes) maps resolver outcomes without treating a denied, locked or interrupted file as an absent or empty document.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.14. Reading and updating resource metadata

requirements.text: To update default-Version attributes, the client writes Version Properties and calls `Labels.AddAttribute` or `Labels.RemoveAttribute` against the Version's `Epoch`. To update Resource Meta attributes, it writes meta Properties and calls the corresponding Method on `MetaLabels` against `MetaEpoch`. A Resource Meta label change MUST increment `MetaEpoch` and update `MetaModifiedAt`. It MUST NOT change Version `Epoch` or `ModifiedAt` unless the interaction also changes Version attributes.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.14. Reading and updating resource metadata

requirements.text: Base Properties such as `Epoch`, `CreatedAt`, `ModifiedAt`, `MetaEpoch`, `MetaCreatedAt` and `MetaModifiedAt` are normally server-managed and MUST NOT be directly writable unless the server explicitly allows administrative writes.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.14. Reading and updating resource metadata

requirements.text: To change the default Version, the client uses the domain Property or Method mapped to xRegistry `defaultversionid`. The base mapping is the logical Resource's `VersionId`; it does not define a separate `DefaultVersionId` Property. A successful change MUST increment `MetaEpoch` and update `MetaModifiedAt`. It changes the delegated normal Properties and the target of future logical Resource opens. The change MUST NOT alter the logical Resource NodeId or `Xid`, any exact Version NodeId or `Xid`, or any node's deletion role.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.14. Reading and updating resource metadata

requirements.text: `MetaDefaultVersionSticky` maps Core `defaultversionsticky`. When true, creating or removing another Version does not automatically replace the selected default; when false or absent, the Core `versionmode` rule selects the default. Core rejects a true value when the Resource type sets `maxversions` to `1`; the OPC UA Property does not weaken that constraint. If a sticky selected Version is deleted, the Server selects the newest remaining Version as REQUIRED by the companion model. A default change updates Resource Meta only, not either Version's `Epoch`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.14. Reading and updating resource metadata

requirements.text: `MetaReadonly` maps Core `readonly`, whose default is false. It is read-only to non-admin clients; the binding does not define how a Server identifies an admin client. `MetaCompatibility` maps the OPTIONAL Core `compatibility` value. `MetaDeprecated` maps the OPTIONAL Core `deprecated` object using `DeprecationDataType`: `Effective` and `Removal` are `DateTime`, and `Alternative` and `Documentation` are `UriString`. The Server MUST preserve these field types and presence; it MUST NOT encode the object as a String or as an `AttributesType` label.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.14. Reading and updating resource metadata

requirements.text: Deleting the meta view is not supported. The server MUST reject attempts to delete the meta view with `Bad_NotSupported` or `Bad_InvalidArgument`. Individual mutable meta attributes, including entries in `MetaLabels`, MAY be reset through update processing if the domain model supports them.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.15. Replacing a resource document

requirements.text: Resource document replacement creates the Resource if needed, then replaces the selected default Version's complete document. For an absent logical Resource, the client preferably calls `GetOrCreateResource` on the parent Group. Strict `CreateResource` rejects an existing exact `(ResourceId, VersionId)` pair; it does not reject every existing logical Resource, because a new Version can be added to one. It then opens the logical Resource or returned exact Version for writing, uses Write plus EraseExisting to stage a complete replacement, writes the complete new byte stream and closes the handle. It writes or validates exact Version metadata Properties. Complete replacement MUST truncate any previous content: `Open(mode = 6)` combines Write and EraseExisting. Merely setting the file position to zero does not remove a longer previous suffix. For replacement, the client can request no creation-time handle and then Open with mode 6. If it already holds a creation-time write handle without documented truncation semantics, it closes that handle without changes and reopens with mode 6.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.15. Replacing a resource document

requirements.text: Partial patching of document bytes is not defined. A client that wants to change document content MUST provide a complete replacement document.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.16. Deleting resources

requirements.text: To delete a document-backed Resource, the client calls its `Delete(ExpectedEpoch: UInt32)` Method. Supplying `0` disables the check. A non-zero `ExpectedEpoch` MUST equal the logical Resource's current `MetaEpoch`, not its delegated Version `Epoch`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.16. Deleting resources

requirements.text: Each `Delete(ExpectedEpoch)` Call targets one selected logical Resource. A server MUST NOT retain any exact Version from a deleted Resource as a detached or group-level alias.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.18. Creating and updating versions

requirements.text: To create or update a Version, the client resolves its exact `ResourceType` under the logical Resource's `Versions` component. If absent and creation is allowed, the client calls `GetOrCreateResource` on the Group with the Resource and Version identifiers, or `CreateResource` for strict creation. The returned `ResourceNodeId` identifies the exact Version; `AssignedVersionId` supplies its assigned identifier. That Version's BrowseName MUST be its `versionid`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.18. Creating and updating versions

requirements.text: For partial metadata updates, only named version attributes are written. For full version representations, omitted mutable attributes are reset or removed according to xRegistry rules. String labels on `ResourceType` MAY be managed through `Labels.AddAttribute` and `Labels.RemoveAttribute` on the exact Version's `Labels` `AttributesType` object where supported. Typed extension attributes use `NativeRegistryAccessType` or a domain mapping.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.18. Creating and updating versions

requirements.text: Adding a Version to an existing Resource MUST increment the Resource's `MetaEpoch` and update `MetaModifiedAt`, whether or not the new Version becomes the default. Modifying an existing Version updates that Version's `Epoch` and `ModifiedAt` but MUST NOT by itself change the Resource's `MetaEpoch` or `MetaModifiedAt`. If the same interaction also changes Resource Meta or the default Version, those Resource Meta changes follow §5.14.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.18. Creating and updating versions

requirements.text: If an empty version map is supplied for a non-existent resource, the server MUST reject it with `Bad_InvalidArgument`, corresponding to xRegistry `missing_versions`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.19. Reading a version

requirements.text: A client reads Version metadata by Reading that exact Version's Properties. Its `Xid` MUST be the logical Resource `Xid` plus `/versions/<VID>`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.21. Deleting versions

requirements.text: To delete a Version, the client calls the exact Version Object's `Delete(ExpectedEpoch: UInt32)` Method. Supplying `0` disables the check. A non-zero value MUST equal that Version's `Epoch`. Only that exact Version is removed. To delete a Versions collection subset, the client uses a sequence or server-defined batch of `Delete(ExpectedEpoch)` Calls targeting exact Versions selected by `VersionId`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.21. Deleting versions

requirements.text: A server MUST reject deletion of the last remaining version of a resource if the xRegistry model requires every resource to have at least one version. A server MUST also reject deletion of a default version unless it can atomically select a new default or the request explicitly sets one through a supported flag or meta update.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.21. Deleting versions

requirements.text: If the version is the default version, the server MUST either reject the delete with `Bad_InvalidState` or update default-version state according to xRegistry and domain rules.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 5. Registry operations / 5.21. Deleting versions

requirements.text: Removing a Version from a surviving Resource MUST increment the Resource's `MetaEpoch` and update `MetaModifiedAt`. This applies whether or not deletion selects a new default Version. It does not increment any surviving Version's `Epoch` unless that Version's own attributes are also modified.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Request flags

requirements.text: When xRegistry defines a flag as a response-shaping hint, a server SHOULD ignore it if unknown or unsupported. If the flag is needed for safe write semantics, the server MUST reject an unknown or unsupported value with `Bad_NotSupported` or `Bad_InvalidArgument`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Request flags

requirements.text: | [`inline`](https://github.com/xregistry/spec/blob/v1.0-rc4/core/spec.md#inline-flag) | Browse and Read the named child collections or Properties in the same client operation sequence. A domain export MAY inline server-side |

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Request flags / 6.1. Filtering

requirements.text: The common federation selector looks up label keys as Core map keys and compares values as Core case-insensitive strings. Requested values are literal, including `*` and the empty string; an absent label does not match. The client MUST NOT impose NFC normalization or mandatory language labels. Before claiming unique selection, it needs every necessary Browse page and Property read. BrowseName namespace indexes and Browse order do not supply label values.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Request flags / 6.2. Ignore processing

requirements.text: Standard Write and Call requests carry no arbitrary xRegistry option map. A generic client needing `ignore` semantics MUST use a server-defined operation accepting write options, or MUST omit the ignored attributes from the representation before issuing standard Writes and Calls.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Request flags / 6.2. Ignore processing

requirements.text: Unsupported ignore requirements MUST fail with `Bad_NotSupported` or `Bad_InvalidArgument`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Request flags / 6.4. Sorting

requirements.text: Browse order alone MUST NOT be assumed to be xRegistry sort order unless the server explicitly documents that behavior in `Capabilities`. Version order is conveyed by attributes such as `ancestorid`, `createdat` and `defaultversionid`, not by container position. A server MAY expose a domain index Property if it needs deterministic order.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Request flags / 6.5. Document and metadata modes

requirements.text: The `meta` flag selects Property access for Resources and Versions. The logical Resource supplies Resource and Resource Meta views; an exact Version supplies the Version view. A client MUST NOT use metadata mode to attempt byte-level partial document updates.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 6. Request flags / 6.6. Pagination and ranges

requirements.text: Continuation points are session-scoped OPC UA state and are not serializable as stable xRegistry identifiers. A protocol bridge MAY translate between another binding's pagination tokens and OPC UA continuation points internally.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 7. Value encoding

requirements.text: Strings MUST be encoded as OPC UA `String`, timestamps as `DateTime`, integer epochs as `UInt32`, and labels as `String` Property Variables under `Labels` or Resource Meta `MetaLabels`. Federation targets are `ExpandedNodeId`, and document bytes are `ByteString` chunks returned by `Read` on `FileType`. Native-document numeric fields retain their declared exact numeric types. In particular, an authored epoch in `RegistryMetadataDataType` uses `RegistryNumberValueDataType`; it MUST be an integer within the UInt32 range before commit. The Property mapping does not change that native ABI.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 7. Value encoding

requirements.text: A server MUST preserve unknown typed extension attributes that it accepts in the native document or a domain mapping. It MUST use `Labels` or `MetaLabels` only for string-valued labels. If it cannot preserve an accepted extension attribute, it MUST reject the update rather than silently losing information.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 8. Serialization / export-import / 8.1. Native metadata and navigation

requirements.text: Without a defined retrievable Core API URL, metadata MUST use document-local navigation. `self` locates the entity within the returned JSON document, not within the OPC UA AddressSpace. For example, in a whole-Registry export, an asset's `self` is `#/documents/main/assets/item`. Its Meta `self` is `#/documents/main/assets/item/meta`. In a standalone Resource result they are `#` and `#/meta`. Here `#` denotes the empty [RFC 6901 JSON Pointer][json-pointer] selecting the document root. The XID remains `/documents/main/assets/item` in either result.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 8. Serialization / export-import / 8.1. Native metadata and navigation

requirements.text: Every emitted local pointer MUST resolve within that returned document. Use JSON Pointer escaping for path components. Convert `metaurl`, `defaultversionurl` and collection URLs to local pointers when their targets are included, and never append `$details`. Core permits collection URL/count attributes to be omitted in document view. Where a selected Core shape requires a navigation target, the exporter MUST include that target or use a defined API URL. If neither is available, it MUST report `unsupported_operation`, not fabricate an `opc.tcp` URL or dangling pointer.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 8. Serialization / export-import / 8.2. Core document-view export

requirements.text: A whole-Registry export MUST apply the Core `doc` and requested `inline` semantics, including the following:

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 8. Serialization / export-import / 8.2. Core document-view export

requirements.text: - Keep a local `xref` as the source Resource's identity and `meta.xref`. When its same-Registry target is accessible, expose the Core-derived target attributes under the source identity; do not substitute the target's ID, XID or self reference, or follow a target `xref` transitively. If the target is inaccessible or dangling, expose only the source identity and `meta.xref`; no local Version storage is REQUIRED. Requests for an alias's Versions in document view retain `cannot_doc_xref`, mapped to `unsupported_operation` by a resolver.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 8. Serialization / export-import / 8.2. Core document-view export

requirements.text: - Include the requested collections, including empty maps, after completing their Browse continuation sequences. OPTIONAL counts, if emitted, MUST describe the included collection.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 8. Serialization / export-import / 8.2. Core document-view export

requirements.text: - Preserve OPTIONAL/empty labels and typed extension attributes. Do not coerce a structured catalog advertisement into a label string.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 8. Serialization / export-import / 8.2. Core document-view export

requirements.text: For an included, document-bearing Version, use `<RESOURCE>` or `<RESOURCE>base64` according to Core. An exact-byte export SHOULD use raw FileTransfer bytes and `<RESOURCE>base64`, including `""` for a zero-byte document. JSON domain bytes are not the Resource's metadata. Reserializing JSON does not preserve its original byte representation. Metadata-only Versions MUST NOT gain `<RESOURCE>`, `<RESOURCE>base64` or a fake domain URL.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 8. Serialization / export-import / 8.2. Core document-view export

requirements.text: `ResourceUrl` maps only to Core `<RESOURCE>url` when it actually identifies the domain document with a defined retrieval mechanism. Preserve external documents as links when exporting a linked representation. An offline-complete export MUST obtain and include all declared documents in its scope under policy. It MUST NOT claim completeness from locators alone. `ExternalReference` is not a Core JSON attribute. A documented extension can preserve it as native provenance, or a permitted document read can materialize its bytes, but it MUST NOT become `meta.xref`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 8. Serialization / export-import / 8.2. Core document-view export

requirements.text: The baseline export makes multiple calls without an atomic snapshot. Default selection, membership, Properties or document bytes can change between calls. If traversal is incomplete or an inconsistency is detected, the exporter MUST invalidate any complete, consistent-export claim. Sections 10.4 and 11.1 define the resolver outcome.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 8. Serialization / export-import / 8.2. Core document-view export

requirements.text: Serialization MUST preserve the three-representation symmetry defined by the xRegistry Primer and the Version 0.11.0 companion model. An entity keeps the same `Xid` and identity when accessed as a file, through OPC UA Services or in an exported xRegistry document.

requirements.text: Within an interaction, the server MUST emit at most one event for each canonical type and `Subject`. For a given `Subject`, it MUST also emit at most one of `created`, `updated` or `deleted`. requirements.text: The server MUST determine the complete event set from the committed result before reporting any event. Recursive deletion reports version leaves before their resource containers, resources before their group containers, and groups before the registry event. Events are reported only after the deletion commits, through a notifier that survives the deletion. Event payloads MUST reflect the committed result and MUST NOT expose a partial intermediate state.

Subtypes MAY add intermediate notifier Objects if the Server-to-Version path specified above remains available.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.3. Three distinct reference mechanisms

requirements.text: A local `xref` MUST remain the case-sensitive XID of a same-typed Resource in the same Registry, represented by `MetaXref`. It MUST NOT be an absolute URI or remote-node locator. Structurally identical Resource definitions do not establish a shared type. Imported/shared types follow Core [`ximportresources`](https://github.com/xregistry/spec/blob/v1.0-rc4/core/model.md#reuse-of-resource-definitions). When the target is accessible, the Server exposes the Core-derived target view under the source Resource's identity while retaining the source `ResourceId`, `Xid`, self reference and `MetaXref`. It MUST NOT follow a target `xref` transitively. When the target is inaccessible or dangling, the source identity and `MetaXref` remain readable; the Server is not REQUIRED to detect the condition or provide local Version storage. The source's minimal serialization remains valid. `ExternalReference` MUST NOT substitute for `MetaXref`.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.3. Three distinct reference mechanisms

requirements.text: A Resource describing remote bytes retains local metadata. Remote `Xid`, `ResourceId`, `VersionId`, labels or Meta values MUST NOT silently overwrite that local describing entity. To read the remote Registry intentionally, the caller establishes a separate context. A domain can explicitly define logical-identity relationships; equal XIDs in unrelated Registries do not establish one.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.3. Three distinct reference mechanisms

requirements.text: An unsupported retrieval scheme or undocumented convention MUST fail explicitly. Implementations MUST NOT assume `ResourceUrl` and `ExternalReference` are interchangeable spellings of one target. If both are present, a declared mapping and policy determine their relationship and selection. Arbitrary precedence does not resolve conflicting or ambiguous targets.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.3. Three distinct reference mechanisms

requirements.text: `XREG-GroupFederation` is a separate OPTIONAL facet. A Group reference owns read-only `OriginRegistry`, `ExternalReference` and `GroupUrl` Properties. Its source key includes the trusted origin, collection-qualified Group XID and Group role. Selection MUST verify the remote `GroupType` ancestry, REQUIRED domain subtype, XID and Registry ownership. A Resource, Version or Registry root MUST NOT substitute for that Group. `GroupUrl` is only an authorized locator. The referencing server maps the verified remote Application URI through its own `ServerArray`; setting `ServerIndex` to zero does not make a remote target local. A native Group metadata identity claim MUST agree with the independent Group observation. Epoch rollback, or different metadata at an already observed epoch, MUST fail without replacing the last verified observation.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.4. Trust and live consistency

requirements.text: Catalog metadata, discovered endpoints and remote references supply untrusted locators, not trust decisions. The resolver checks destination, transport, application certificate and authorization at every hop. Credentials, user identity tokens and file handles MUST NOT be forwarded to a remote Server by implication. After a policy, integrity or version failure, the resolver MUST NOT weaken security or silently try another advertisement.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.4. Trust and live consistency

requirements.text: The server MUST persist immutable origin selection and portable remote identity with the owning logical Resource's federation record. Restore MUST validate the exclusive origin form, agreement with its trusted binding, XID, target role and portable Node identities. It MUST NOT silently repair contradictory records, persist Session-local indexes as identity pins or reinterpret an origin change as relocation. Restoring pins does not authenticate a peer; fresh provider and Session checks precede use. Group federation records follow the same origin and portable-identity rules.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.4. Trust and live consistency

requirements.text: A live Browse/Read/FileTransfer capture MUST retain its scope and observations and disclose that it has no cross-node atomic snapshot guarantee. A pinned native document view guarantees only the selected document and authorization view under §4.5, not a transaction over remote providers or separately opened domain files. If a consistent capture is requested, changed membership, default selection, table mapping, metadata or file contents during capture MUST produce `inconsistent_snapshot`. Per-node timestamps alone cannot establish cross-node atomicity.

source.section: xRegistry OPC UA API - Version 1.0-rc4 / 10. Federation / 10.4. Trust and live consistency

requirements.text: The OPTIONAL [publication extension](../publication/spec.md) provides retained exact Version documents rather than inferring a snapshot from these live indicators. Its descriptors select Registry access with `binding: "opcua"`, the endpoint and the parameters in §10.1, followed by an exact Version XID. Resolve that Version under the selected Registry root using §4.2, then read its raw document bytes using §5.13.1. This applies to the manifest and captured Registry JSON as well as domain documents. A captured Registry JSON Version is not the live multi-read export in §5.3. No HTTP facade, HTTP GET or standard UA context node is needed.

If the adapter cannot represent the Meta extensions or obtain a coherent head, it MUST report the operation as unsupported or inconsistent instead of substituting the default Version or a live view.
